title: Who should pack the parameters
impact: Moonshot: rejected, but the mechanism works and the reason it still loses is the useful part. `executeBatch` sends the writer a `List<List<Object?>>` — 200,000 slots for the Wide Batch Insert shape — which the VM copies before the writer packs the rebuilt graph into a native arena. Packing that arena on the isolate that issued the write and sending its address instead removes the copy entirely, and it is faster on every batch shape measured: -23.6%/-21.9% on a 10k x 8 integer matrix, -13.6%/-13.1% on 10k x 4 ASCII, -7.8%/-7.6% on the 10k x 20 mixed release shape, -19.4%/-18.8% inside `db.transaction`, across two order-flipped collections from separate AOT bundles. It is rejected on where the saving comes from. The price harness shows `SendPort.send` alone is 91-99% of the whole graph copy, so the parameter hop is already paid almost entirely by the sending isolate — in a Flutter app, the UI isolate. The candidate does not remove main-isolate work, it exchanges serialize for pack, and the exchange rate is 0.81x for a fixed-width numeric matrix but 4-5x for anything holding text. Measured as event-loop blocking, a 10k x 20 batch takes the main isolate from 1.2 ms to 5.7 ms of continuous unavailability (+371%), against a library whose contract is zero main-isolate jank. The numeric matrix is the one shape that wins both metrics and it has no representative incidence: both release batch lanes bind text in every row. Two findings outlive the rejection — the parameter graph copy is 5.6-17.0% of a batch write and the sender pays essentially all of it, so any proposal to change what crosses the writer boundary is trading main-isolate time and can be costed in minutes; and event-loop blocking, which no release lane reports, is the metric this library's contract is actually about. Runtime reverted; prototype at `archive/exp-280`; both harnesses retained as `benchmark/experiments/batch_param_transport_price.dart` and `batch_param_arena_ab.dart`.
